about: Hester is named mostly as a vocative inside an old man's speech, each followed by 'he said'; only three narration sentences show her as 'She'.
title: The Goat Gate
author: Ada Pell

chapters.title: Evening
paragraphs: "Hester, close the gate before the goats get out," the old man called from the porch.
"Not now, Hester," he said when the dog began to bark.
Hester latched the gate and walked up the path. She carried the milk pail in both hands.
"Hester, the lamp," he said, and pointed at the dark window.
"Yes, Hester, the big one," he added, as if the lamp might have been forgotten.
The kitchen smelled of smoke and onions. The old man sat by the stove and rubbed his knees.
"Hester, will you read to me?" he asked.
Hester took the book from the shelf. She opened it at the ribbon and began to read aloud.
The clock ticked over the stove. The goats settled in the shed. Outside the wind moved through the orchard.
"Good night, Hester," he said at last, and closed his eyes.
Hester put the book away. She banked the fire and climbed the stairs with the candle.
In the morning the gate was open again. The goats were in the orchard. Nobody could say how they had got there.
"Hester!" he shouted from the porch, and the whole valley heard it.
